\chapter{An Accident near the Bridge}
\label{ch:gu-an-accident-near-the-bridge}
\hlchaptermodality{293}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say where an accident happened and who was hurt.}

Complete the last lesson of chapter 293: I can say where an accident happened and who was hurt.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{અકસ્માત} (akasmāt)}{અકસ્માત (akasmāt)}]{\gu{અકસ્માત} (akasmāt) — an accident}

\label{lesson:GU-C293-akasmat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a detective, then the Gujarati for to nab.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{અકસ્માત}}
\textbf{\gu{અકસ્માત}} — \emph{akasmāt} — \textquotedblleft{}an accident\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{ગઈકાલે} \gu{સાંજે} \gu{પુલ} \gu{પાસે} \gu{મોટો} \gu{અકસ્માત} \gu{થયો}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{gaīkāle sā̃je pul pāse moṭo akasmāt thayo.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Yesterday evening there was a big accident near the bridge.
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{અકસ્માત}} (\emph{akasmāt}) is Sanskrit \emph{akasmāt}, \textquotedblleft{}without a why or a wherefore, suddenly\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), used in Gujarati as a noun: what happens without warning. It is masculine: \textbf{\gu{અકસ્માત} \gu{થયો}}, there was an accident.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{akasmāt}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{akasmāt}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gaīkāle sā̃je pul pāse moṭo akasmāt thayo.} — Yesterday evening there was a big accident near the bridge.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for a detective, then the Gujarati for to nab, then say \emph{akasmāt} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{અકસ્માત} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An accident\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{ટક્કર} (ṭakkar)}{ટક્કર (ṭakkar)}]{\gu{ટક્કર} (ṭakkar) — a collision}

\label{lesson:GU-C293-takkar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for to nab, then the Gujarati for an accident.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{ટક્કર}}
\textbf{\gu{ટક્કર}} — \emph{ṭakkar} — \textquotedblleft{}a collision\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{બસ} \gu{અને} \gu{ગાડીની} \gu{ટક્કર} \gu{થઈ}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bas ane gāḍīnī ṭakkar thaī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A bus and a car collided.
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
goes back to \emph{ṭakkarā}, \textquotedblleft{}a blow on the head\textquotedblright{}, and CDIAL lists Gujarati \emph{ṭakkar}, \textquotedblleft{}a blow\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 5424). Two vehicles have a \textbf{\gu{ટક્કર}}: \textbf{\gu{બસ} \gu{અને} \gu{ગાડીની} \gu{ટક્કર} \gu{થઈ}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭakkar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭakkar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bas ane gāḍīnī ṭakkar thaī.} — A bus and a car collided.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for to nab, then the Gujarati for an accident, then say \emph{ṭakkar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{ટક્કર} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A collision\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{ઘાયલ} (ghāyal)}{ઘાયલ (ghāyal)}]{\gu{ઘાયલ} (ghāyal) — injured}

\label{lesson:GU-C293-ghayal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for an accident, then the Gujarati for a collision.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{ઘાયલ}}
\textbf{\gu{ઘાયલ}} — \emph{ghāyal} — \textquotedblleft{}injured\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{આ} \gu{અકસ્માતમાં} \gu{ત્રણ} \gu{લોકો} \gu{ઘાયલ} \gu{થયા}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ā akasmātmā̃ traṇ loko ghāyal thayā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Three people were hurt in this accident.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{ઘાયલ}} (\emph{ghāyal}) is built on \emph{ghāy}, a wound, from Sanskrit \emph{ghāta}, \textquotedblleft{}a blow\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists Gujarati \emph{ghāyo}, a wounded person, under that word (CDIAL 4460). A person \textbf{\gu{ઘાયલ} \gu{થાય} \gu{છે}}, gets hurt.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ghāyal}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ghāyal}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ā akasmātmā̃ traṇ loko ghāyal thayā.} — Three people were hurt in this accident.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for an accident, then the Gujarati for a collision, then say \emph{ghāyal} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{ઘાયલ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Injured\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{ગંભીર} (gambhīr)}{ગંભીર (gambhīr)}]{\gu{ગંભીર} (gambhīr) — serious}

\label{lesson:GU-C293-gambhir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a collision, then the Gujarati for injured.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{ગંભીર}}
\textbf{\gu{ગંભીર}} — \emph{gambhīr} — \textquotedblleft{}serious\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{એક} \gu{છોકરાને} \gu{ગંભીર} \gu{ઈજા} \gu{થઈ}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ek chokrāne gambhīr ījā thaī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
One boy was seriously injured.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{ગંભીર}} (\emph{gambhīr}) is a tatsama, Sanskrit \emph{gambhīra}, \textquotedblleft{}deep\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams). In Gujarati it is a deep, grave matter: \textbf{\gu{ગંભીર} \gu{ઈજા}}, a serious injury; \textbf{\gu{ગંભીર} \gu{માણસ}}, a serious man.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gambhīr}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gambhīr}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ek chokrāne gambhīr ījā thaī.} — One boy was seriously injured.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for a collision, then the Gujarati for injured, then say \emph{gambhīr} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{ગંભીર} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Serious\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{ગભરાવું} (gabhrāvũ)}{ગભરાવું (gabhrāvũ)}]{\gu{ગભરાવું} (gabhrāvũ) — to panic}

\label{lesson:GU-C293-gabhravu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for injured, then the Gujarati for serious.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{ગભરાવું}}
\textbf{\gu{ગભરાવું}} — \emph{gabhrāvũ} — \textquotedblleft{}to panic\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{અકસ્માત} \gu{જોઈને} \gu{ડ્રાઈવર} \gu{ગભરાઈ} \gu{ગયો}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{akasmāt joīne ḍrāīvar gabhrāī gayo.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
When he saw the accident, the driver panicked.
\end{quote}

Past (he …): \gu{તે} \gu{ડ્રાઈવર} \gu{ગભરાઈ} \gu{ગયો}, \emph{te ḍrāīvar gabhrāī gayo}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{ગભરાવું}} (\emph{gabhrāvũ}) probably comes from \emph{*ghabbhara}, \textquotedblleft{}confused\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs, under which it lists Gujarati \emph{ghābhrũ}, \textquotedblleft{}confused\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 4427). It is to lose your head with fright: \textbf{\gu{ગભરાઈ} \gu{ગયો}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gabhrāvũ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gabhrāvũ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{akasmāt joīne ḍrāīvar gabhrāī gayo.} — When he saw the accident, the driver panicked.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for injured, then the Gujarati for serious, then say \emph{gabhrāvũ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
